summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares preinstall=`node setup.mjs`. On `npm install`, setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes that Bun binary against `math_init.js`, a 727KB single-line obfuscator.io-style bundle shipped in the tarball (rotated string array, opaque char/opcode table, decoder function, marked `// @bun @bun-cjs`). Executing the payload under a separately-fetched runtime rather than under Node is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern, and defeats Node-level inspection of the actual install-time behavior. The package advertises itself as `Verdocs Web SDK for React` but is published under the unrelated `@hubsync/` npm scope; the `dist/` tree is a benign stencil-generated Verdocs web-sdk shell, and the installer-harm behavior lives entirely in the preinstall dropper. Installing this package runs attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
